user.title: Choose your utility
user.description: Pick the utility company that provides your energy data. Only utilities currently supported by the Open Green Button proxy server are shown.

connect.title: Authorize with {utility_name}
connect.description:
**Step 1.** Open the authorization link below in a new tab and complete the Green Button consent flow with {utility_name}.

[Authorize {utility_name} →]({authorize_url})

**Step 2.** After consent, the page shows a code starting with `gb_live_`. Paste it below.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authorize {utility_name}
reauth_confirm.description:
Your authorization with {utility_name} has expired or was revoked. Re-authorize by opening this link in a new tab:

[Re-authorize {utility_name} →]({authorize_url})

After consent, paste the new claim code below.

error.cannot_connect: Cannot reach the Open Green Button server. Check your internet connection and try again.
error.claim_code_empty: Paste the claim code shown on the authorization page after consent.
error.invalid_or_expired_code: This claim code is unknown, expired, or already used. Open the authorize link again to get a fresh code.

abort.already_configured: This utility account is already configured.
abort.cannot_connect: Cannot reach the Open Green Button server.
abort.no_utilities: The Open Green Button server has no utilities configured.
abort.unknown_utility: The selected utility is no longer available.

init.title: Polling schedule
init.description: Your utility tells the Open Green Button server how often it may be polled, and that cadence is always respected. When it works out to once a day, you can choose which time of day that poll runs.

data.daily_poll_time_enabled: Poll daily at a specific local time

data_description.daily_poll_time_enabled: Turn this off to poll once every 24 hours counted from when Home Assistant last started. Utilities that allow more or less frequent polling ignore this setting.
data_description.daily_poll_time: Uses Home Assistant's local timezone and follows daylight-saving changes. If Home Assistant is down at this time, the poll runs when it next starts.

background_load_pending.title: {utility} is preparing your data
background_load_pending.description:
{utility} answered the data request with "collecting it now, it'll be available later" (HTTP 202) instead of returning it straight away. That's a normal mode for some utilities — it isn't an error, and it doesn't mean anything is misconfigured.

Open Green Button is re-checking every few minutes and will import the data as soon as your utility releases it. **No action is needed.** This notice clears itself on the first successful import.

If it's still here tomorrow, the message will change to say so.

background_load_stuck.title: {utility} still hasn't delivered the data it promised
background_load_stuck.description:
{utility} said it was preparing your data (HTTP 202) more than a day ago, and it still hasn't been delivered. Open Green Button has been re-asking with the same request the whole time, which is what the utility needs in order to hand back the batch it prepared.

This one we'd like to see. Please use the **Learn more** link below to open the tracking issue on GitHub and add a comment with: your utility/energy provider and region, how much history you were importing, and whether this is a residential or commercial account. Enabling debug logging for the integration first (Settings → Devices & Services → ⋮ → Enable debug logging) captures your utility's own response, which is the part we can't get any other way.

rebuild_statistics.name: Rebuild statistics
rebuild_statistics.description: Deletes this account's imported energy and cost statistics, then re-downloads and recomputes them from scratch. Use this after an update changes how usage or cost is calculated. Does not require re-authorizing with your utility.

config_entry_id.name: Account
config_entry_id.description: Which Open Green Button account to rebuild. Leave empty to rebuild every configured account.
